newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brazil buys 88 tanks from Belgium for $15 million.
newsitem.headline: Brazil buys 88 tanks from Belgium for $15 million.

text.p: Brazil has bought 88 surplus Leopard tanks from Belgium for $15 million, the Belgian defence ministry said on Friday.
"We sold 88 tanks including seven for the spare parts," Colonel Ronny Vandenbroele told Reuters.
Brazil will receive the German-built tanks by the end of 1998. They will replace M-41 tanks which it bought in the 1950s.
Vandenbroele said Germany delivered the tanks in 1969 and 1970 and they have twice been modernised -- to instal target tracking and computer systems.
Belgium, which bought 334 Leopard tanks altogether, is selling a wide range of military equipment following a drastic army restructuring and freeze on new defence spending.
Chile, which bought 25 second-hand French Mirage fighter planes for 1.6 billion francs ($47 million) in July 1994, may also buy another 77 of the German-built Leopards that are on sale, he said.
Belgium has also sold 11 Leopards to Norway for 88 million francs ($2.6 million) while Mexico bought anti-tank equipment.
But plans to sell surplus surface-to-air missiles to Turkey were frozen last month following increased tension over Cyprus.
